text: Machine learning is a way for computers to learn from data without being explicitly programmed. One common type is supervised learning, where the computer uses labeled training data. This data contains examples with both inputs and the correct outputs. The computer studies these examples to build a model, which is like a set of rules or patterns. Once the model is ready, it can make predictions on new, unseen data. For instance, it might predict whether an email is spam based on past emails. The model's accuracy is measured by comparing its predictions to the actual results. Higher accuracy means the model has learned the patterns well. As more data becomes available, the model can be improved and become even more reliable.
